item.title: How to Read a Business Partnership in Zi Wei Dou Shu: The Sibling, Friends and Children Palaces Together
item.description: A partnership cannot be judged by how well you get along; read the Sibling Palace, traditionally the partnership palace, the Friends Palace for partners and subordinates, and the Children Palace for the partnership and splitting money. If these palaces are struck by Ji or hold heavy malefics, the cooperation brings disputes and should not be forced. Final rights, duties and accounts should rest on a professional lawyer and a written contract.

item.title: How to Read Buying a Home in Zi Wei Dou Shu: The Property Palace First, with Installments and Contract Details Checked Item by Item
item.description: Buying a home is a major matter; read the Property Palace mainly for fixed assets and dwelling luck, then the Wealth Palace for affordability. Wen Chang and Wen Qu often correspond to installments and loans, while Ju Men with Hua Ji warns against traps in contracts, title and verbal promises. The palaces are reference; before buying, review the contract item by item, verify the title and take on debt within one's means, not swept up by a bargain.

item.title: How to Read Huo Xing and Ling Xing: One Bursts, One Grinds, Both Can Spark
item.description: Huo Xing and Ling Xing are both fire and among the four malefics: Huo Xing arrives fast and bursts, showing suddenness, haste and clash; Ling Xing comes hidden and grinds long, showing prolonged resentment and entanglement. Alone they are malefics, but they can also become a spark of force, as Huo Xing with Tan Lang forms Fire-Tan; the key is knowing their difference and giving the force an outlet.

item.title: How to Read Po Jun and Lian Zhen in the Spouse Palace: A Changeable Relationship, Adjust Before Promising
item.description: Po Jun or Lian Zhen in the Spouse Palace often means more change in feelings: Po Jun is bold and easily seeks novelty, while Lian Zhen has a changeable mind and emotional swings, and with malefics the relationship is less stable. The key is not a hasty verdict of separation but adjusting fully and confirming stability before promising, treating the changeable stage as a process of understanding.

item.title: How to Read Qing Yang in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Impulsive Punishment or Decisive Execution
item.description: Qing Yang is metal and transforms into punishment, one of the four malefics: fallen and guarding the life it often means a hasty, argumentative nature that clashes head-on; strong and restrained it means decisiveness and the ability to achieve where judgment is needed. The key is separating impulsiveness from decisiveness and channeling the force into execution with discipline and buffers.

item.title: How to Read Tai Yang in the Spouse Palace: A Responsible Partner, Family vs. Everyone
item.description: Tai Yang in the Spouse Palace often means a responsible, warm partner who willingly takes on family matters, best when strong and with Hua Lu. Yet Tai Yang may give to too many people and seem universally generous; the key is distinguishing responsibility to the family from generosity to everyone and guiding that warmth back to the small family.

item.title: How to Read Tan Lang in the Spouse Palace: A Fun-Loving Partner, Freshness Takes Effort
item.description: Tan Lang in the Spouse Palace often means a charming, fun-loving partner who values quality of life and freshness, and the relationship often begins with strong attraction. Over time, without interaction and ritual it can feel flat; the key is treating freshness as something to maintain rather than misjudging it as fickleness.

item.title: How to Read the Decade-Year Overlap in Zi Wei Dou Shu: A Ten-Year Theme Meets a One-Year Trigger
item.description: To judge when something happens, the key is the decade-year overlap: the decade limit governs the ten-year theme and focus, while the year governs the concrete trigger. When the same line, such as spouse, property or career, is activated in both the limit and the year, the timing is strongest and the matter most easily lands in that year.

item.title: How to Read the Double-Lu Flanking Pattern: Resources Around You, and Where They Come From
item.description: Double-Lu Flanking places Lu Cun and Hua Lu in the two palaces on either side of the Life Palace, signaling that resources, opportunity and help with money are often close. It does not mean gain without work; see which palaces the two lu fly from and whether Hua Ji breaks them.

item.title: How to Read the Fire-Tan Pattern in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Sudden Gain vs. Keeping It
item.description: The Fire-Tan pattern pairs Tan Lang with Huo Xing, supported by Lu Cun or Hua Lu, and signals sudden opportunity and self-made gains. Whether you keep that windfall depends on the Wealth and Karma palaces and later limits, not a guarantee of riches.

item.title: How to Read the Four Layers in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Constitution, Climate, Trigger and Flashpoint
item.description: Reading time uses four layers: the natal is the innate constitution and foundation, the decade is the ten-year climate, the year is the trigger, and the month or day is the flashpoint where the matter concentrates. In inference the flowing stars take priority, layered natal, decade, year, month, so you both see the big trend and pin down the specific month.

item.title: How to Read the Killing-Surrounding-Lian-Zhen Pattern: Achieving Amid Change
item.description: Killing-Surrounding-Lian-Zhen places Lian Zhen and Tan Lang guarding the life in Si or Hai, with Wu Qu and Qi Sha meeting from You or Mao, formed by four stars. It signals a life of many changes that can achieve in specialized, unconventional or highly competitive fields, depending on star strength and the mix of auspicious and malefic.

item.title: How to Read the Romance Stars: Hong Luan, Tian Xi, Xian Chi, Tian Yao, Healthy Romance vs. Trouble
item.description: The romance stars in Zi Wei include Hong Luan, Tian Xi, Xian Chi, Tian Yao and Mu Yu: Hong Luan and Tian Xi mostly indicate proper romance, marriage and happy occasions, while Xian Chi and Tian Yao lean toward charm, desire and social attraction. The romance stars are not inherently bad; the key is whether malefics share the palace to create romance trouble, and whether emptiness stars or Tian De resolve it.

item.title: How to Read the Yang-Liang-Chang-Lu Pattern: A Strength for Study and Exams
item.description: Yang-Liang-Chang-Lu places a strong Tai Yang and Tian Liang with Wen Chang and Lu Cun in the triple-direction, favoring study, exams, research and public-service work. Whether Wen Chang joins naturally in the trine or is merely pulled from the opposite palace changes the strength, and many malefics break it.

item.title: How to Read Tuo Luo in Zi Wei Dou Shu: The Hidden Force of Delay Can Become Deep Persistence
item.description: Tuo Luo is metal and transforms into Ji, governing delay, repetition, hidden matters and going in circles, often making things feel stuck or slow. Yet it also brings steadiness, persistence and tolerance for repeated refinement, suiting research, practice and deep technical work. The key is turning delay into directed persistence rather than being trapped by it.

item.title: How to Read Wu Qu in the Spouse Palace: A Loyal, Practical Partner Who Should Say the Care Aloud
item.description: Wu Qu in the Spouse Palace often means a practical, loyal, responsible partner who tends to express care through action and material support, but whose emotional expression is rational and can seem cold. The relationship steadies with maturity and shared goals, and the key is turning action-based care into expression the other can feel.

item.title: How to Read Zi Wei in the Spouse Palace: A Strong-Willed Partner, Later Marriage and Mutual Respect
item.description: Zi Wei in the Spouse Palace often means a capable, strong-willed partner who values face and standing; the relationship is best settled after both are mature, often favoring later marriage. The key is mutual respect rather than a contest for dominance, and you should check whether Zi Wei has the hundred-officers support.

item.title: How to Tell Real from False Patterns in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Four Conditions Must Hold
item.description: Whether a pattern truly forms cannot be judged by its name alone; check whether the main stars are strong, assistant stars meet, malefics break it, and transformations activate it. All four must hold with pure energy for a real pattern; fallen stars with heavy malefics and no auspicious stars or transformations is usually a false pattern in name only.

item.title: What to Do When the Birth Hour Is Uncertain in Zi Wei Dou Shu: Reverse-Confirming the Chart
item.description: Zi Wei Dou Shu is sensitive to the birth hour; one slot off and the Life Palace and stars can change entirely. When the hour is uncertain, do not guess; set a range, then use the person's character, appearance, career and past major events such as schooling, marriage, moves, illness and losses to verify year by year, reverse-deriving the hour that best fits, which is fixing the chart.

item.title: Zi Wei Dou Shu vs. Ba Zi: A Spatial Star Map and a Five-Element Balance
item.description: Zi Wei Dou Shu and Ba Zi both use birth time but differ in approach: Zi Wei places stars into a spatial map of twelve palaces and reads the star combinations, using the lunar calendar; Ba Zi uses stems and branches to derive five-element strength and balance, using solar terms. They excel at different questions and can be cross-referenced.

item.description: A Gregorian month can cross a lunar month boundary. Check the chart setting and event date before reading November's monthly cycle.

item.title: Body Palace vs Life Palace: Baseline vs Adult Focus
item.description: The Life palace is the innate temperament and lifelong baseline. The Body palace is lodged in one of six palaces—Life, Spouse, Wealth, Travel, Career or Blessing—and points to where adult effort lands and where you are most engaged.

item.title: Born After 11 PM: Early and Late Rat Hour and Comparing Two Charts
item.description: The Rat hour runs from 23:00 to 01:00. One school advances the lunar day at 23:00 when the Rat hour begins, while another keeps the part before midnight as the late Rat hour of the current day. For 23:00–24:00 births the two rules yield different lunar days, so in practice chart both and reverse-check against lived events rather than committing to one school in advance.

item.title: Do Daylight Saving and True Solar Time Affect the Chart? Check Longitude, DST and Leap Months
item.description: Clocks follow a uniform time zone, while the birth hour is set by local solar time at the birthplace, so longitude matters. Mainland China observed daylight saving from 1986 to 1991, so records from those years must first be shifted back one hour. Leap months, lunar phases and solar-term boundaries must not be mixed. For births near a boundary, comparing two charts is safest.

item.title: How to Determine the Birth Hour: Compare Two Charts and Verify
item.description: When the birth hour is uncertain, first chart each possible hour. If born within about fifteen minutes of a boundary, lay the two charts side by side and reverse-check against major events already lived—education, relocation, job changes, marriage or childbirth, and health turns—using the relevant decade and year. Whichever fits the record better is the chart to use.

item.title: How to Read an Empty Life Palace: Borrow the Opposite Palace
item.description: When none of the fourteen major stars sits in the Life palace, it is an empty palace: borrow the major stars of the opposite Travel palace, then combine the three-ways-four-corners and the helpful or harsh stars. An empty palace means the baseline is shaped by environment, not that the chart is weak.

item.title: How to Read Buying a Home: Property Palace as the Wealth Treasury
item.description: The Property palace governs real estate, the home environment and the wealth treasury, and it is linked to the Wealth palace as one root. For buying a home, first read the Property palace major stars and brightness and whether Hua Lu or Lu Cun is present, then read the Wealth palace and where Hua Ji falls to see whether cash flow holds, and use the decade and year for timing. This is a tendency reference, not investment advice.

item.title: How to Read the Three-Ways-Four-Corners: Life, Wealth, Career and Travel
item.description: From any palace, the three-ways-four-corners joins its two trine palaces and the opposite palace. For the Life palace, these are Wealth, Career and Travel together with Life. Judge a domain by the stars and transformations across this whole group, not a single palace.

item.title: How to Read the Twelve Palaces in Order: Anchor on Life
item.description: The twelve palaces are not read in a queue. Anchor on Life, first read the core group of Life, Wealth, Career and Travel, then enter the palace matching your question—Spouse, Property, Blessing and so on—and link them through the three-ways-four-corners.

item.title: How to Tell a Real Zi Wei Pattern: A Four-Element Check
item.description: A named pattern is not real just because the stars line up. Check four elements: whether the major stars are bright, whether helpful stars like Zuo Fu, You Bi, Tian Kui and Tian Yue meet, how heavily harsh stars break it, and whether the four transformations activate it. All four make a real pattern; fallen stars with harsh stars and no activation are usually only a name.

item.title: Hua Lu and Hua Ji in Opposition: Palaces, Clashes and Layers
item.description: Hua Lu is resources, opportunity and ease, while Hua Ji is contraction, blockage and a lesson. When they land in opposite palaces or clash in the same three-ways, see which sits in the Life core and which is activated in time, and note which layer—natal, decade or year—each falls on. Do not declare success or failure simply because Lu and Ji appear together.

item.title: Is Zi Wei Dou Shu Accurate? It Shows Tendencies, Not Fixed Fate
item.description: Zi Wei Dou Shu describes the temperament tendencies and event probabilities shown by star combinations. It helps you understand your patterns and plan ahead, but it does not decide outcomes. Accuracy depends on a correct chart and birth time, and on whether the reading is layered and verifiable rather than absolute or promising to change fate.

item.title: Layering Decade Transformations Over the Natal: Lu Broken and Ji Meeting Ji
item.description: The decade-stem transformations land on the natal chart and layer with the natal transformations and palaces. When decade Hua Ji clashes the natal Hua Lu palace, it is Lu broken by a clash—ease can turn into change. When decade Hua Ji enters the natal Hua Ji palace, the lesson deepens and must be faced directly. When decade Lu, Quan or Ke meet natal positive palaces, the decade runs more smoothly.

item.title: Natal, Decade and Yearly Four Transformations: Static vs Timed
item.description: The birth-year-stem four transformations are fixed static indicators of lifelong themes and are not good or bad by themselves. The decade-stem transformations govern only ten years and the yearly-stem transformations only one year; they are timed activations. For a yearly reading, focus on the decade and year groups, and give weight to the natal group only when it is activated.

item.title: The Fire-Star and Tan Lang Pattern: Conditions and Timing
item.description: The Fire-Star and Tan Lang pattern (and its Ling Xing version) needs Tan Lang in Life, Wealth, Career or Travel, sharing a palace with Huo Xing or Ling Xing or meeting them in the three-ways. Sharing a palace, sitting in Chen, Xu, Chou or Wei, and gaining Lu Cun, Hua Lu, Ke or Quan raises the level. It points to sudden opportunity, but a matching decade or year must activate it; the stars alone do not trigger it.

item.title: The Zi Wei and Tian Fu Same-Palace Pattern: Conditions to Form
item.description: Zi Wei and Tian Fu share a palace only in Yin or Shen, but sharing is not enough. The three-ways need Zuo Fu and You Bi as a base, with Tian Kui, Tian Yue, Lu Cun, Hua Lu and Wen Chang or Wen Qu adding strength. If Kong Jie and heavy Hua Ji break it, the pattern is hollow and ambition can outrun ability.

item.title: What Temple, Thriving, Favorable and Fallen Mean for Major Stars
item.description: Temple, Thriving, Favorable and Fallen describe how strongly and steadily a star expresses in a palace. Temple and Thriving express the star well, while Fallen is less steady and needs support, but Fallen is not automatically bad, and Temple still depends on transformations and harsh stars.

item.title: What to Read First in a Zi Wei Dou Shu Chart: A 5-Step Order
item.description: After generating a Zi Wei Dou Shu chart, do not jump palace by palace. Set the tone with the Life and Body palaces, then the three-ways-four-corners and natal four transformations, before the twelve palaces and finally the decade and yearly cycles.

item.title: Which Palaces to Read for a Business Partnership: Friends and Children
item.description: Partnership is read mainly through the Friends (Servants) palace and the Children palace. When Friends sends Hua Lu, Quan or Ke to meet the Life three-ways, partners tend to help; when Friends Hua Ji clashes the Life palace, partnering is unwise. The Children palace covers shareholders, equity and subordinates, and Children Hua Ji clashing Life also argues against taking a share. The chart only shows tendencies; in practice, use a written agreement, define equity and spell out the exit.

item.title: Why Patterns Are Set by the Life Palace Three-Ways, Not Other Palaces
item.description: A pattern describes the overall structure and level of a person, and the Life palace is the hub, with Wealth, Career and Travel as its trine and opposite forming the main axis. Spouse, Children and Friends are topic palaces; they can form a small pattern within that domain, but they cannot define the lifelong major pattern.
